children: will be announcing earnings results this Tuesday after market hours. Here’s what to look for.

NXP Semiconductors beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $3.50 billion, up 19.5% year on year. It was a strong quarter for the company, with a meaningful improvement in its inventory levels and a decent beat of analysts’ operating income estimates.
Is NXP Semiconductors a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting NXP Semiconductors’s revenue to grow 18.7% year on year, a reversal from the 2.4% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. NXP Semiconductors rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at NXP Semiconductors’s peers in the semiconductors segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Texas Instruments delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 27.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 2.6%, and Penguin Solutions reported revenues up 67.7%, topping estimates by 8.8%. Texas Instruments traded down 1.9% following the results while Penguin Solutions was up 13.1%.

Over the last year or so, investors' attention has moved from one major market theme to the next, spanning AI disruption and surging infrastructure investment to geopolitical tensions, interest rates, and the health of the broader economy. While some of the semiconductors stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 13.7% on average over the last month. NXP Semiconductors’s stock price was unchanged during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $305.28 (compared to the current share price of $235.29).

Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.

title: Earnings to watch: NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) reports Q3 results tomorrow
